title: 5 tips to sleep quick & deep
summary: Five tips to fall asleep faster and sleep better: get cold before bed, time meals to exploit post-meal drowsiness, cut caffeine and late pre-workouts, keep the bedroom and lying down sacred, and stop letting stress and anxiety about insomnia follow you to bed. He opposes sleeping pills.
claims: Sleep is the most underrated part of recovery; perfect diet, training and low stress mean nothing without enough good sleep
Sleep quality matters as much as quantity: a short optimized night can beat a long poor one
Sleep need is largely genetic; most adults stabilize around 7-8 hours and need less with age
Find your sleep need by sleeping without alarm, light or noise when not sleep-deprived or on stimulants
You fall asleep better with low body temperature: sleep in a cool room with the window open
Take a cold shower before bed, staying until you're cold to the bone; especially effective in summer
He gets sleepy for an hour after any meal; schedule your last meal shortly before bed if food makes you drowsy
A carb-heavy meal can strengthen post-meal sleepiness
A huge meal before bed makes him wake up starving
He doesn't drink coffee; he tried it once, felt nothing and dislikes stimulants
Most people drink more coffee than they think, and even a noon cup affects sleep
Caffeine borrows energy you don't have, builds tolerance and creates a coffee-insomnia cycle
A pre-workout at 7 pm for an 8-9 pm session wrecks sleep; better performance is worthless if recovery suffers
Bodybuilding is about what the weight does to your muscles and how they recover, not the weight lifted
Blue light doesn't bother him because he respects the other tips; susceptible people should avoid screens before bed
Make the bedroom sacred: no phone, TV or laptop, and keep pets out if you can
He only lies down when he goes to sleep, so lying down immediately makes him sleepy
Reserve lying down for bed so the position becomes a sleep trigger
Much insomnia is psychological: fear of not sleeping triggers it, like recurring panic attacks
'Don't think about anything' is bad advice; let your mind drift freely instead
Being 'too lazy to sleep' and staying up past your window is your own fault
Don't obsess over sleep cycle lengths; go to bed as early as you can and focus on quality
He does not recommend sleeping pills; fix your body yourself instead of taking drugs
